headline: Roblox expands AI game creation and adds offline/browser play
summary: Developers can now use natural language prompts to build games, which will also be playable outside the Roblox platform.
details: Roblox is making significant strides in empowering its creators with new tools and expanded reach. The platform is rolling out its generative AI game creation feature, 'Build', more broadly, allowing users to create games using natural language prompts. This feature is expanding beyond its initial limited release and gaining desktop access and new asset libraries.

A key development is the ability for creators to make their games available as standalone apps on mobile, PC, and consoles, with Roblox serving as the underlying game engine. Furthermore, by the end of the year, players will be able to access games directly through a web browser via a link, extending the reach of Roblox experiences beyond the main platform.

To enhance the building process, Roblox is introducing new NPC capabilities, including AI-powered playtesting. Creators will also be able to implement an offline mode, ensuring uninterrupted gameplay even in areas with poor network connectivity.

Roblox is also focusing on improving the player experience with a new Friends chat tab that moves with the player and supports voice typing. An enhanced discovery algorithm will tailor game suggestions based on user age and playtime preferences.

For 2D game development, Roblox is introducing features like orthographic cameras and direct sprite-sheet import for animation. Additionally, within its 'Moments' feed, players will soon be able to tap on avatars to purchase in-game items.

Financial tools for creators are also being enhanced. Since 2013, Roblox creators have earned over $5 billion. The new Roblox Wallet, in partnership with Airwallex, will allow creators to receive earnings in real money daily and transfer funds to bank accounts. A Roblox Card is also planned for launch next year.

These announcements underscore Roblox's dual focus on increasing player engagement on its platform, which saw players spend over 29 billion hours last quarter, and expanding the accessibility and reach of user-generated content.
